claims.claim_vi: The source traces an order: the client places it via the broker app, the broker sends it to the exchange, the client gateway validates, rate-limits, authenticates and normalizes, the order manager does risk checks per the risk manager's rules and checks funds in the wallet, the matching engine emits two executions per match, and orders and executions are sequenced so replay is deterministic; the executions are returned to the client; the trading flow (steps 1 to 14) is the critical path while market data and reporting flows are not.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19, Python 3: a price-then-time order book on 2,000 random limit orders (price 95 to 105, quantity 1 to 10) produced 1,442 matches (one record per buy/sell pairing, not per side) with total volume 4,373; replaying the same sequence gave an identical list; swapping one random adjacent pair changed the list of matches in 51 of 200 trials; a small example of two sell orders of 5 at 100 then a buy of 7 at 100 filled 5 against the first and 2 against the second.
claims.verified_by: Script run in the session with a fixed seed; results copied from output.

claims.claim_vi: Price-then-time priority is the author's general knowledge of order books and was not matched against a specific exchange's rules.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only).

design_notes_vi: Khung một là năm chặng của luồng giao dịch; khung hai là ba ghi chú. Thử nghiệm nằm trong bài.
source_deviations: The source's fourteen steps are grouped into five stages; the lesson adds a small order-book experiment on replay and on swapping two orders.
The matching rule (price, then arrival time) is the author's general knowledge, not the source's.
